answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring sustained, non-transferable proof of effort. A new identity often sits alone like a single lotus, unable to verify itself. It must prove unique utility across many epochs; its peer-verified record builds a reliable bridge of trust that prevents a single actor from spawning thousands of cheap identities. Only when a node proves its history—anchored at the harbor of consensus—does it gain voting power. This ensures that the economy stays decentralized rather than ruled by mass-generated accounts.
